newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIA CENTRAL BANK RAISES RATES.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIA CENTRAL BANK RAISES RATES.

text.p: Indonesia's central bank, Bank Indonesia, raised interest rates for central bank certificates (SBIs) of all maturities by 100 basis points on Wednesday.
"We have raised interest rates for all papers by 100 basis points," a Bank Indonesia official said.

The central bank raised rates on its overnight bilateral central bank certificates (SBIs) to 15.0 percent from 14.0 percent, rates on two-to-six day SBIs to 16.0 percent from 15.0 percent, one-week to 10.5 percent from 9.5, two-week to 11.0 percent from 10.0, one-month to 11.625 percent from 10.625, three-month to 11.5 percent from 10.5, six-month to 12.125 percent from 11.125, and one-year to

The central bank raised rates on its overnight bilateral central bank certificates (SBIs) to 15.0 percent from 14.0 percent, rates on two-to-six day SBIs to 16.0 percent from 15.0 percent, one-week to 10.5 percent from 9.5, two-week to 11.0 percent from 10.0, one-month to 11.625 percent from 10.625, three-month to 11.5 percent from 10.5, six-month to 12.125 percent from 11.125, and one-year to 12.75 percent from 11.75 percent.
The central bank cut its bilateral SBI rates for papers above one-week by 50 basis points last Friday.
Currency dealers said the move was aimed at containing speculative dollar buying.
